subject: Renewal: Upgrade reserved pool 8→16 GPUs — commit & throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stratusai.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal question — considering 8→16 GPU reserved pool upgrade

Hi Rafael,

Hope you're well. We're starting our renewal planning for the dedicated capacity contract that ends March 1. Over the past quarter our inference traffic has grown ~2.8x and the 8-GPU reserved pool is hitting sustained high utilization during peak hours. We'd like to explore upgrading to a 16-GPU reserved pool at renewal.

A few items we need clarity on before we can sign:
- Updated monthly commit (what would the committed spend look like for 16 GPUs vs the current 8?)
- Throughput guarantees: can Redwood provide baseline throughput/SLOs for our typical workload (avg prompt ~350 tokens, 90th percentile request size ~800 tokens)?
- Phasing options: we may prefer a phased increase across the first 30 days if that helps with our cashflow.
- Any operational changes (onboarding, reserved capacity lead times, maintenance windows) and attachments we should expect for procurement.

We need to finalize terms with Finance by Feb 20. Can you send an initial amendment and a short ops note for procurement? I'm including procurement on cc.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Director of ML Ops
Stratus AI
(attachment: current_usage_report_q4.pdf)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal question — considering 8→16 GPU reserved pool upgrade

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciate the heads-up on timelines; Feb 20 is doable.

High-level proposal (initial):
- Reserved capacity: 16 GPUs (steady-state).
- Monthly commit (16-GPU): $68,000/month (12-month term). This reflects a blended reserved rate plus a modest volume credit vs on-demand.
- Phasing option: we can stage to 12 GPUs for the first 30 days and automatically scale to 16 on day 31. The monthly commit remains for 16 GPUs but we apply a phased uplift credit for month 1 (see attached draft amendment).
- Throughput & operations: targeting 99% availability SLA; baseline throughput guarantee of sustained capacity to support ~40 concurrent 512-token requests with median token latency targets for your model family. We will include a 20% burst buffer for short peaks. Detailed SLA table attached.
- Onboarding and ops: 2-week activation window, runbook handoff, and a single escalation path to our dedicated infra on-call.

I've attached a draft amendment and a proposed SLA table for procurement to review. Marissa (AE) and Karthik (SE) are cc'd to help with commercial and technical follow-ups.

Would you like us to send the DocuSign-ready amendment or handle via your procurement portal?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft_amendment_8to16.pdf)

Looping in Monica for CSM context. Rafael — quick thoughts before we lock pricing:
- Commercial: $68k/month is reasonable but leaves limited room for additional onboarding credits. Recommend offering a $5k one-time onboarding credit and a 5% commit discount if they sign within 7 days.
- Phasing: propose explicit milestones tied to utilization (e.g., move to 16 GPUs once sustained 72-hour avg >70% on 12 GPUs) — helps procurement buy-in.
- Escalation clause: include a 30-day buffer clause for capacity surges and a clear overage rate (per GPU-hour) when burst cap exceeded.

Karthik — can you confirm the technical feasibility of the 20% burst buffer and whether we should tie the throughput SLA to quantization profiles (FP16 vs 4-bit)?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal question — considering 8→16 GPU reserved pool upgrade

Marissa / team — technical notes:
- 20% burst buffer: feasible, implemented as short-lived autoscale slots that draw from a shared burst pool. We should limit continuous burst to 10 minutes to protect other customers and avoid sustained load.
- Throughput SLA: recommend two tiers in the SLA:
  * Tier A: quantized model (4-bit), guaranteed baseline throughput (higher rps, lower latency)
  * Tier B: FP16 / higher-precision model, slightly reduced guaranteed throughput but higher quality
- If they expect a lot of long-context requests (800+ tokens), we need to add a token-based throttling clause — long tails materially reduce effective concurrency.

Attached is a capacity matrix showing expected rps by model family and GPU count. I'm also proposing an operational fallback: automatic routing to compatible model variants if the primary pool is saturated.

Attachment: capacity_matrix_q1.xlsx

Karthik

Alex / procurement team — attaching the finalized amendment and a concise ops note for procurement. Summary of agreed terms below so you can take to Finance: 

Summary of final terms (agreed):
- Reserved capacity: 16 GPUs (dedicated reserved pool).
- Monthly commit: $68,000/month for a 12-month term; we applied a $5,000 one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice).
- Phasing: 12 GPUs for the first 30 days, automatic promotion to 16 GPUs on day 31 OR once a 72-hour sustained >70% utilization on the 12-GPU pool is observed — whichever comes first.
- SLA & throughput guarantees: 99% availability; baseline throughput commitments separated by model family (Tier A — quantized models; Tier B — FP16). We include a 20% burst buffer with a continuous burst cap of 10 minutes; burst beyond this will be billed at agreed overage rates.
- Ops & onboarding: 2-week activation window, runbook handoff, and a 30-day joint run to tune batching/kv-cache settings.
- Next steps: I can send the DocuSign-ready amendment to your procurement portal this afternoon if you confirm procurement@stratusai.com is the right address.

Attachments: draft_amendment_8to16.pdf, proposed_sla_table.csv

Thanks for working through this. If Procurement is good, we'll send the DocuSign and schedule the activation kickoff for the week of Mar 2.
